content: Neosporin is an antibiotic ointment originally developed by Pfizer and later sold to Johnson & Johnson. The name Neosporin is derived from the Greek words neo (new) and sporos (seed). This product is primarily used to prevent infections and promote the healing of wounds. The original formulation of Neosporin contains three antibiotics: bacitracin, neomycin, and polymyxin B. These antibiotics work synergistically to target a broad spectrum of bacteria. Specifically, neomycin and polymyxin B are effective against gram-negative bacteria, while bacitracin is active against gram-positive bacteria. This combination makes Neosporin a triple antibiotic ointment, providing coverage against a wide range of bacterial pathogens that may infect wounds. Despite its efficacy, these antibiotics are generally used only topically because systemic (parenteral) administration can lead to severe side effects, such as nephrotoxicity. Even when applied topically, side effects can occur. Neomycin, in particular, is well-documented for causing allergic reactions, including allergic contact dermatitis. Additionally, while Neosporin is generally safe, it can sometimes intensify the sensation of pain in minor abrasions and external injuries, though this is typically harmless. For individuals allergic to neomycin, Pfizer also produces a related product called Polysporin, which contains only bacitracin and polymyxin B. Since neomycin is excluded, Polysporin is a safer alternative for those with neomycin allergies. Furthermore, Pfizer has introduced Neosporin + Pain Relief, available as both an ointment and a cream. This formulation includes pramoxine, a topical analgesic, to provide pain relief. The cream version omits bacitracin zinc due to its instability in a cream base, making it suitable for individuals sensitive to bacitracin or zinc. In Canada, the Neosporin brand is not sold. Instead, Polysporin is available in various formulations. The original ointments in Canada contain polymyxin B and bacitracin, while creams and eye/ear drops include polymyxin B and gramicidin. A triple antibiotic ointment is also available in Canada, which combines all three antibiotics: polymyxin B, bacitracin, and gramicidin.
